agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Dutch district court judgment (5 February 2020) in a suit by civil-society plaintiffs against the State. Declares Wet SUWI art. 65 and Besluit SUWI chapter 5a, governing the SyRI data-linking and risk-report system, unenforceable toward the admitted plaintiffs as contrary to ECHR Art. 8(2).
summary.long: Judgment of the Hague District Court of 5 February 2020 in a case brought by four collective interest organisations (NJCM, Platform Bescherming Burgerrechten, Privacy First, Koepel van DBC-Vrije Praktijken), with FNV intervening, against the Dutch State. The case concerns SyRI (Systeem Risico Indicatie), a government mechanism in Wet SUWI art. 64-65 and Besluit SUWI chapter 5a, in force from 1 January 2014, under which designated public bodies link datasets in a secure environment to generate risk reports on possible social-security, tax and labour-law fraud. The court found that art. 65 Wet SUWI and chapter 5a Besluit SUWI violate ECHR Art. 8(2) for insufficient safeguards, citing limited transparency about risk indicators and the risk model, no integral prior necessity review, data-minimisation concerns and no duty to notify data subjects. It held that art. 64 Wet SUWI on its own does not violate Art. 8(2). It declared them unenforceable toward the admitted plaintiffs and those whose interests they represent. The Landelijke Cliëntenraad and two individual plaintiffs were declared inadmissible. Claims for disclosure of risk models and for destruction of data were rejected, and the data-processor claim was not reached. The State was ordered to pay costs of EUR 3,250.51.

relations.note: The court states it applies the ECHR and ICCPR provisions as binding under these constitutional articles. Registry ID not verified.

relations.target_text: Wet structuur uitvoeringsorganisatie en inkomen (Wet SUWI), artikel 65 and chapter 5a of the Besluit SUWI
relations.note: The judgment's operative part declares article 65 Wet SUWI, together with chapter 5a Besluit SUWI, unenforceable (onverbindend) toward the NJCM, Platform Bescherming Burgerrechten, Privacy First and Koepel van DBC-Vrije Praktijken, for conflict with ECHR art. 8(2). Article 64 Wet SUWI is not found in conflict (6.110). Registry ID not verified.

notes: Court judgment (first instance, Rechtbank Den Haag), not a statute. Relations describe the legal framework the court applies, not relations created by this text. Target_instrument_id is left empty because registry IDs were not verified. The text does not state whether an appeal was lodged. Internal points: the text spells the claimant organisation as 'NCJM c.s.' once (6.43) and as 'Platform voor Burgerrechten' in the operative part (7.2) and in places elsewhere, versus 'Platform Bescherming Burgerrechten' in the parties section. The Wet SUWI 'Wet van 9 oktober 2013' (footnote 7) is cited as amending the Wet SUWI with effect from 1 January 2014 (4.1).

thresholds.note: The judgment states no numeric cut-off that changes legal treatment. The retention, destruction and feedback periods (two years, four weeks, twenty months) are procedural time limits, coded as events or obligations rather than thresholds. The risk-model cut-off (afsnijpunt) is described only as fixed in advance, with no value given in the text. The count of 17 data categories and the 1 January 2014 effective date are not treatment cut-offs.
